inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 are competing fixes for the same leak (wallet rebroadcast under -privatebroadcast): one routes rebroadcasts through private broadcast, the other suppresses them. They now share a band; #36607, the generic PeerManager-level guard covering both pathways plus submitpackage, should be reviewed first and the choice between the other two made against it.
Chain: #36628 (stateless private-broadcast jobs) is the stated prerequisite for #36608 (same rewrite plus package relay). Review #36628 first; #36608 should not be assessed independently of it.
Chain: #36506 explicitly depends on #36437, which also contains the fuzz harness that demonstrates the hole. Review #36437 first.

Direction conflict: the #36628/#36608 rewrite removes node-side private broadcast state entirely, which would obsolete or rework #34271, #34322, #36477 and #36566 (and possibly #34533/#36330/#36607). A decision on the rewrite should precede detailed review of those incremental patches.
#36477 scored near the bottom alone but is the stated dependency of P1 #36607 (it keeps finished broadcast records in memory so they can be matched); it was raised accordingly.

#36374 and #36637 fix the identical Tor control password backslash bug by different means; #36637 (hex encoding, permitted by the control spec) is the more general and should be reviewed first, after which the other should be closed.

#35502 and #35522 are the same kind of move-only extraction from net_processing (receive side and send side) and were banded differently; they are now both P4 and should be sequenced together, as #35522 was surfaced by review of #34824.
#34824 is not a generic cleanup: it retires recursive mutexes in tx-relay message handling (issue #19303) and feeds the later send-side refactor, so it sits above the other refactors.
#36358 is a backport of #36312 to the 31.x branch; it duplicates work already on master and only matters for the maintenance release.
result.notes: Two large clusters dominate this category and drive most of the band adjustments: the private broadcast work (eight PRs, including a full rewrite that overlaps most of the incremental patches) and the 1p1c/orphanage relay-liveness work (#36437, #36506, #36486, #36578, #36594, #36015). Within P1 I ordered by breadth and certainty of the attack or leak; the remaining spread uses P2 for measurable relay/DoS/privacy value, P3 for narrow but real fixes, tests and refactors with stated payoff, and P4 only for move-only or speculative work.
